data.title: Axis Bank Q2 Results: Net profit jumps 38% YoY- Check asset quality, stock trend, and other key highlights
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- Axis Bank on Saturday, October 17, reported a 38% year-on-year (YoY) jump in net profit to Rs.7,003 crore for the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs.5,089 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The private sector lender's earnings were supported by growth in net interest income and an improvement in asset quality.

Net interest income (NII), the difference between interest earned and interest expended, increased 12% YoY to Rs.15,371 crore. Net interest margin (NIM) stood at 3.36% during the quarter and improved to 3.47% after excluding the impact of foreign currency non-resident (FCNR-B) deposits.

Operating profit grew 6% YoY to Rs.11,083 crore, while core operating profit rose 11% to Rs.10,998 crore. Other income declined 1% to Rs.6,531 crore, even as fee income advanced 6% to Rs.6,381 crore.

Commenting on the bank's performance, managing director and CEO Amitabh Chaudhry said Axis Bank continued to focus on digital payments, secure banking, AI-driven innovation and strategic partnerships to strengthen its customer offerings.

Axis Bank reported a year-on-year improvement in its asset quality, with the gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio falling 30 basis points (bps) to 1.16% in Q2FY27. The net non-performing asset (NNPA) ratio declined 9 bps to 0.35%.

Gross slippages dropped to Rs.4,762 crore during the September quarter, compared with Rs.5,566 crore in the preceding quarter and Rs.5,696 crore a year earlier. The net slippage ratio also declined 30 bps YoY to 0.75%.

The lender's annualised net credit cost came in at 0.45%, marking a reduction of 28 bps year-on-year and 18 bps sequentially. Meanwhile, its provision coverage ratio remained stable at 70%, unchanged from both the previous quarter and the corresponding period last year.

Axis Bank set aside Rs.1,694 crore towards provisions and contingencies in Q2FY27, including Rs.1,564 crore in specific loan-loss provisions.

As of September 30, 2026, the bank had accumulated Rs.15,860 crore in provisions against standard assets and additional provisions outside those for non-performing assets (NPAs). These were over and above the NPA provisions accounted for in the calculation of its provision coverage ratio.

Axis Bank's advances expanded 23% year-on-year and 9% quarter-on-quarter to Rs.13.74 lakh crore as of September 30, 2026.

Retail lending increased 16% YoY to Rs.7.40 lakh crore, representing 54% of net advances. SME loans grew 25% to Rs.1.65 lakh crore, while corporate lending registered growth of 34%.

Total deposits rose 21% year-on-year and 6% sequentially to Rs.14.52 lakh crore on a month-end basis. Term deposits recorded 27% growth, while current account deposits increased 7% and savings account deposits advanced 12%.

The current account and savings account (CASA) ratio stood at 36%. The bank's cost of funds also declined by 8 bps from the year-ago period.

Axis Bank's capital adequacy ratio stood at 16.27% as of September 30, 2026, while its common equity tier-1 (CET-1) ratio was 14.61%. The bank added 23 bps to its CET-1 ratio during the first half of FY27.

In addition, the lender held Rs.8,006 crore in provisions over and above those reflected in its reported capital adequacy ratio. These additional provisions represented a capital cushion equivalent to approximately 49 bps.

For the first half of FY27, Axis Bank's net profit climbed 30% year-on-year to Rs.14,117 crore from Rs.10,896 crore in H1FY26.

NII increased 10% to Rs.30,018 crore, while fee income rose 6% to Rs.12,536 crore. Operating profit advanced 4% to Rs.22,742 crore from Rs.21,928 crore in the year-ago period.

Core operating profit grew 11% to Rs.22,120 crore compared with Rs.20,010 crore in H1FY26.

Axis Bank shares ended Friday's session, October 16, at Rs.1,290, up 0.16%, ahead of the Q2FY27 earnings announcement.

The stock has gained around 4% over the past month but has declined 1.5% over three months and 4.5% over six months. Over the past year, it has advanced approximately 8%.

On a year-to-date basis, Axis Bank shares have gained 1.2%, outperforming the Nifty 50, which has fallen 11.5% over the same period. The lender's market capitalisation stood at approximately Rs.4.02 lakh crore.

Investors will track the bank's net interest margins, loan growth, deposit mobilisation and asset quality in assessing the sustainability of earnings growth and the stock's outlook.

data.title: Steve Eisman Warns OpenAI Is Now So Important That Its Collapse Could Cause A Recession In The US
data.description:
Key points:
  • Eisman said the scale of capital flowing into AI has made OpenAI much more important to the economy than many investors may realize.
  • He highlighted the capital expenditure commitments being made by cloud providers, chip companies and infrastructure firms to support the AI boom.
  • Eisman said that if demand for AI services suddenly weakened, the effects could ripple through the companies supplying that infrastructure.

“The Big Short” investor Steve Eisman is raising a fresh warning about the growing importance of artificial intelligence to the U.S. economy, arguing that OpenAI has become so deeply embedded in the AI investment boom that a collapse at the company could have consequences far beyond the technology sector.

Speaking on The Compound and Friends podcast on Friday, Eisman said the rapid growth of OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies has created an unusual concentration of economic and financial risk.

OpenAI Has Become ‘Systemically Important’

Eisman said the scale of capital flowing into AI has made OpenAI much more important to the economy than many investors may realize.

“If OpenAI went bankrupt tomorrow, and I'm not making that prediction, but let's just say that it did, I think the US economy would go into recession immediately,” Eisman warned.

He questioned how quickly an AI company could become so important to the broader economy.

Eisman highlighted the capital expenditure commitments being made by cloud providers, chip companies and infrastructure firms to support the AI boom. If demand for AI services suddenly weakened, the effects could ripple through the companies supplying that infrastructure, he explained.

AI Faces A Price War As ‘Token Maxing’ Ends

Eisman also sees a potential pressure point emerging inside the AI industry itself, which is falling prices.

He argued that the economics of the leading AI models are becoming increasingly difficult to sustain as cheaper open-weight models improve and customers begin scrutinizing their AI budgets.

“There's pretty good evidence that a price war is starting,” Eisman said.

He pointed to the rapid decline in the cost of running AI models and the emergence of open-weight alternatives as a major threat to companies trying to maintain premium pricing.

“You've got open weight models that are a tenth the price. They're not as good as the models, but you know, you don't need a Mercedes-Benz for every road trip,” he said.

Eisman believes the end of “token maxing”, which refers to companies spending aggressively on AI usage without closely scrutinizing the economics, could expose the industry's underlying vulnerabilities.

“They were making more money as a result of token maxing than they reasonably could have made on an ongoing basis once companies looked at their budgets and said, we obviously can't spend at this rate on AI as great as the technology is,” he said.

‘It’s All One Trade’, Says Eisman

For Eisman, the biggest concern extends beyond OpenAI itself. He sees the AI boom as increasingly interconnected, with major technology companies and infrastructure providers depending on continued AI spending.

“The problem with the AI story is a concentration problem,” Eisman said.

He specifically pointed to Nvidia Corp.’s (NVDA) customer concentration, arguing that the chipmaker’s exposure to a handful of major customers highlights how tightly connected the AI ecosystem has become.

But Eisman’s broader warning is about what happens to financial markets if the AI narrative changes. “There is only one narrative that matters right now, and that's AI,” he said. Eisman ultimately framed AI as the dominant trade driving markets, meaning a major reversal could have consequences well beyond individual AI companies.

“So, you tell me what happens to the AI narrative and I'll tell you what happens to the stock market,” he said. “It’s all one trade. It’s AI. Period. End of discussion.”

Eisman stressed that he is not predicting an OpenAI bankruptcy. He also said that while a major AI downturn could produce a bad recession, he does not view it as comparable to the 2008 financial crisis.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, declined 0.26; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) edged lower by 0.27%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) fell 0.21%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘bearish’ territory at the time of writing.

The Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF (AIQ) fell about 3.2% on Friday, while the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (IYW) fell nearly 3%.

data.title: India's HDFC Bank Q2 profit rises 4.7%; deputy MD Bharucha to step down
data.description:
By Ashwin Manikandan

India's largest private-sector lender, HDFC Bank , reported a second-quarter profit on Saturday that narrowly missed analyst expectations, as weaker treasury income and higher provisions for bad loans offset strong lending growth.

The lender also said in a regulatory filing that its deputy managing director Kaizad Bharucha will step down at the end of December.

The news comes days before a leadership change at the Mumbai-based lender. Anup Bagchi, a veteran of the ICICI group, takes over as managing director and CEO for three years from October 27, becoming HDFC Bank's first external chief executive.

Bharucha, who has been with HDFC Bank for over three decades, was one of two contenders for the top job, Reuters had reported.

Bagchi takes charge amid increased scrutiny of the bank's governance, profitability and operational performance.

The lender posted a standalone net profit of 195.10 billion Indian rupees ($2.05 billion) for the quarter ended September 30, compared with 186.41 billion rupees a year earlier.

Analysts had estimated a profit of 195.26 billion rupees, according to data compiled by LSEG.

Treasury trading gains fell to 7.8 billion rupees from 23.9 billion rupees a year earlier, weighing on earnings despite broad-based loan growth.

Other income, which includes gains on bonds and other investments, fell 3.6% to 138.31 billion rupees.

Indian lenders reported strong credit growth in the quarter across corporate and retail loans.

HDFC Bank's net interest income rose 9.7% to 346.19 billion rupees, with total loans up 16.3%. Deposits grew 18.8% from a year earlier, and the credit-to-deposit ratio stood at 96.0%.

Provisions for potential bad loans and other contingencies rose 2.1% to 35.74 billion rupees.

Asset quality improved. The gross non-performing asset ratio was 1.11% at the end of September, compared with 1.17% at the end of June.

($1 = 94.9600 Indian rupees)

data.title: Circle Targets 40 New Markets As USDC Push Moves Beyond Crypto Trading
data.description:
TL;DR: Circle plans to expand USDC infrastructure into approximately 40 developing and emerging markets. The company is targeting international payments and access to digital dollars rather than relying solely on cryptocurrency exchange demand.

Circle is looking well beyond cryptocurrency trading as it prepares to extend USDC’s reach into approximately 40 emerging and developing markets.

CEO Jeremy Allaire outlined the ambition during discussions surrounding the October 16 international financial meetings in Bangkok. The strategy focuses on places where businesses and individuals want access to dollar-denominated payments but may face expensive or inefficient conventional banking arrangements.

The opportunity is straightforward: a stablecoin that can move between compatible wallets at any hour could offer a useful payment alternative. The difficult part is connecting those wallets to actual financial activity.

From Exchange Balances To Everyday Payments

USDC has long been widely used by cryptocurrency traders as a dollar-linked asset. Circle now wants to make it part of cross-border invoices, business settlement and consumer payments.

That requires more than issuing tokens. Businesses need reliable local currency conversion, banking connections, compliance arrangements and confidence that USDC can be redeemed as intended.

Circle has increasingly built partnerships around these services. Existing stablecoin initiatives, including creator payouts and digital payment programmes, show how digital dollars can be incorporated into familiar financial experiences.

Expansion Will Be Uneven

Regulation is likely to determine the pace of Circle’s international push. Some countries welcome stablecoin payment infrastructure, while others restrict foreign currency access or require substantial local licensing.

Tether’s USDT is also already entrenched across a number of international markets.

Circle must therefore establish the practical value of USDC for customers who may never buy Bitcoin or speculate on another cryptocurrency. If the strategy succeeds, its next stage of growth could depend less on crypto market cycles and more on the ordinary movement of money.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: Polymarket sees 31% chance of S&P 500 hitting 8,000 by year-end
data.description:
Prediction market Polymarket puts the probability of the S&P 500 crossing 8,000 by the end of 2026 at 31%. The benchmark closed at 7,659.44 on Friday, October 16, after gaining nearly 2% for the week despite a sell-off in technology and semiconductor stocks. A move to 8,000 would require a gain of around 4.4% from Friday’s close.

The S&P 500’s earnings outlook remains a key pillar of the bull market. According to FactSet, Q3 earnings are projected to grow 29% year-on-year, while full-year 2026 earnings growth is forecast at 32.8%. Revenue growth for the third quarter is estimated at 12.6%.

Just 9% of S&P 500 companies had reported their third-quarter results as of the latest available data. Of those, 84% beat earnings per share (EPS) estimates, above the five-year average of 78%. However, the aggregate earnings surprise was only 2.6%, well below the five-year average of 7.5%.

That makes the coming weeks crucial: investors will look for evidence that earnings strength extends beyond a handful of large companies and that AI investments are translating into sustainable profits.

Oil, yields and AI concerns threaten the rally

The biggest challenge for equities remains the combination of higher energy prices and persistent inflationary pressure. Brent crude climbed to $110 a barrel on Friday for the first time since May, as escalating Middle East tensions, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and fresh concerns over Russian energy supplies heightened fears of further disruptions.

Investors are also reassessing the sustainability of the AI-driven rally, with concerns over spending, financing and returns on heavy AI investments weighing on chipmakers and technology stocks.

In its latest GREED & fear note, Jefferies warned that global AI stocks’ earnings growth is expected to slow sharply over the next two years, urging investors to look beyond the AI trade for opportunities.

Read More: Jefferies warns AI earnings growth to slow sharply in next 2 years, urges investors to diversify

In a report titled “Diversifying Beyond AI”, Jefferies said consensus earnings growth for AI-related stocks in the MSCI AC World Index is projected to decline from around 100% in 2026 to 30% in 2027 and moderate further to 22% in 2028.

Fed policy remains crucial

Investors have pared back bets on a rate hike at the Federal Reserve’s October 27–28 policy meeting. Comments from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh at the International Monetary Fund’s annual meeting did not dislodge expectations that rates will remain unchanged at the end of the month.

The Fed’s next move, the trajectory of crude prices and the ability of corporate earnings to meet elevated expectations will be key factors in determining whether the S&P 500 can advance towards 8,000 before the year ends.

data.title: HDFC Bank's Kaizad Bharucha to exit on December 31 after over three decades
data.description:
HDFC Bank Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha has sought to step down from the bank’s service with effect from the close of business hours on December 31, 2026, the lender said in a stock exchange filing on Saturday, October 17.

The bank’s Governance, Nomination and Remuneration Committee (GNRC), at its meeting on October 16, and the board of directors, at its meeting on October 17, accepted Bharucha’s request, which will be forwarded to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for approval.

The bank said the committee and board placed on record their appreciation for Bharucha’s contribution over an association spanning more than three decades. It particularly acknowledged his role in conceptualising, establishing and developing the bank’s credit architecture, which it described as one of its defining institutional strengths.

Bharucha joined HDFC Bank in October 1995 and became Deputy Managing Director in April 2023. He has been responsible for several businesses, including retail assets, rural banking, small and medium enterprises, emerging corporates and corporate banking.

Bharucha's exit follows HDFC Bank CEO succession race

Bharucha’s exit comes after he emerged as a leading internal contender to succeed Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Sashidhar Jagdishan, who is due to step down at the end of his term on October 26, 2026.

Media reports in August and September said HDFC Bank had considered Bharucha alongside an external candidate for the top job. The bank subsequently confirmed that it had submitted two names to the RBI but did not disclose the candidates’ identities.

Bharucha joined the bank’s board in 2014 and is its longest-serving executive board member, according to the bank’s website. Reports had also noted that regulatory tenure limits could affect his eligibility for a full three-year term as chief executive.

The company did not state the reason for Bharucha’s decision to leave or disclose the identity of the candidates submitted to the RBI.

data.title: The Silicon Valley Job That Demands Three Years of 24/7 Hustle — WSJ
data.description:
By Katherine Bindley and Chip Cutter

The job requirements are straightforward if not hellacious: Work at the office in person from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Be available "around-the-clock," including nights and weekends if needed. Oh, and you must maintain this schedule for three years.

So goes the criteria for a role working as chief of staff to Vinod Khosla, founder of Khosla Ventures, the renowned venture firm that's backed companies including OpenAI, Stripe and DoorDash.

"If you need predictable hours, a defined playbook, or frequent direction, this isn't for you," wrote Ryan Batra, a vice president of talent at Khosla, in a LinkedIn post about the role.

The chief of staff job listing is either an "amazing opportunity" or indentured servitude, depending on whom you ask. Matteo Franceschetti posted on X that he would take the job himself if he weren't busy running sleep-technology startup Eight Sleep. The entrepreneur and Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian wrote that the job with Khosla was a role that could change someone's life.

Silicon Valley has always been known for the rise and grind. But the AI era is pushing the tech industry's work ethos to new, more visible heights. Rather than something to be played down, working yourself to the bone is to be bragged about — and advertised for up front.

"It's saying the quiet part out loud," says Margaret O'Mara, a professor of history at the University of Washington who writes and teaches about the high-tech economy.

Young AI founders have embraced the so-called 9-9-6, claiming to work from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. six days a week. Corgi, an insurance startup, has asked some candidates to participate in multiday work trials, sometimes on weekends, to test their stamina. Startup LemonLime earlier this year offered interviews to anyone at a networking party willing to get inked with a company tattoo (There was no guarantee of a job, though).

Some saw Khosla's list of requirements, including the minimum 12-hour days, as emblematic of today's no-hire job market, where employers can flex their power — and be explicit in their demands.

"This is the right time for him to be asking for this type of person. Otherwise, these people might have had a lot more options," said Raheela Anwar, a longtime corporate adviser and president and CEO of Group 360 Consulting.

Candidates must consider whether putting up with Khosla's demands will pay off longer term through opportunities that could follow, she added.

"It isn't the job," Anwar said. "It's the exit that is making this attractive."

The chief of staff role has long been a fast track to top positions, making it attractive to high achievers anyway. The job typically requires a mix of both grunt work — sitting in meetings and writing briefs — along with higher-level strategy tasks. Executives usually prefer to hire someone internally, tapping a trusted lieutenant proven at navigating an organization.

Khosla's job description notes the chief of staff will serve as a "thought partner," evaluating possible investments, working with portfolio companies and building relationships.

"You won't know every field I work in," wrote Vinod Khosla in a post to X about the person who will ultimately work for him. "What matters is how quickly you learn, the questions you ask, and whether you can think from first principles."

The job often draws those wanting an up-close view into how an executive operates, even if it requires working around the clock. Jason Fried, the co-founder and CEO of software company 37signals, generally opposes the excesses of tech hustle culture. But he didn't take issue with Khosla's job posting. "The expectations are very clear," he said.

"If I was 25," he added, "maybe it'd be the best thing in the world."

As to whether the pay is commensurate with the required work commitment, only Khosla Ventures knows: It didn't include a salary range in the posting. Based on early interest, Khosla expects more than 1,000 applications, a spokeswoman said.

Late Friday, Vinod Khosla clarified a few details in a post to X: "Jokes aside honest truth is this job has no specific hours requirement but is intense. I work 80 hours/week and this person needs to keep up."

Khosla alumni say the experience alone is worth the job.

"Can't express enough how amazing of a learning experience this is," Hesam Motlagh, a startup founder and adjunct professor at Stanford University, wrote on LinkedIn.

Motlagh would know: He was in the role from 2021 to 2023.

Write to Katherine Bindley at katie.bindley@wsj.com and Chip Cutter at chip.cutter@wsj.com

data.title: The Holdouts Working Around New York City's Airbnb Crackdown — WSJ
data.description:
By Kate King | Photography by Mikey Gulcicek For WSJ

New York City three years ago enacted one of the country's strictest crackdowns on short-term rentals, which reduced the number of listings across the five boroughs by more than 90%.

Most hosts on Airbnb and other online-booking companies abruptly pulled their listings from the platforms after a new law enabled the city to enforce longstanding regulations on rentals of fewer than 30 days.

A small number of homeowners, however, are sticking it out. As of June, more than 3,500 hosts were registered with the city for short-term rentals.

At least another 9,000 are hosting guests for 30 days or longer, allowing them to bypass many of the city's regulations that apply to shorter stays.

The Wall Street Journal spoke with several New York City homeowners who continue to host Airbnb guests about their experiences.

Williams lives with her sisters in the bottom unit of her three-family townhouse. She used to rent out one of the upper apartments on Airbnb for a few days or maybe a week at a time. But after the 2023 law took effect, Williams started hosting guests for 30 days or longer.

Joy's yellow brick and white limestone home is located in the historic Strivers' Row neighborhood, named for the culturally significant residents who have clustered there since the Harlem Renaissance in the early 1900s. Musicians ranging from composer Will Marion Cook to the rapper Tupac Shakur, and former Congressman Adam Clayton Powell, Jr. all lived there.

Williams's guests have included professors and other academics associated with New York schools, including nearby Columbia University, as well as visiting grandparents, summer interns and traveling nurses.

Still, her occupancy rate has declined to about 60% from over 80% and she brings in half the income she did with short-term rentals.

The problem is that bookings rarely line up perfectly, one after another, leaving periods where her unit is sitting empty. If one guest leaves on Sept. 15 and the next guest isn't scheduled to arrive until Oct. 1, for example, Williams loses out on two weeks' worth of potential rental income due to the 30-day minimum stay requirement.

"My preference would be to have the ability to do short-term rental," she said. "I could fill in the blanks."

Soni and his wife invested more than $30,000 gut-renovating and furnishing their home's ground-floor apartment for their parents' monthslong visits from India. They bought an expensive mattress, installed a new stove and work station and fully stocked the kitchen with dishes and appliances.

To help pay their mortgage, they rent out the unit on Airbnb for 30 days or more during the nine to 10 months a year it isn't occupied by family.

But finding a tenant for a month hasn't been easy. Before the city's crackdown took effect, Soni earned an average $25,000 a year hosting short-term guests through Airbnb. Bookings dropped significantly after he switched to longer stays.

Soni hasn't been able to raise his rental rate in three years to cover his property's rising insurance, upkeep and utility expenses.

Most frustratingly, Soni regularly fields requests from acquaintances and former guests offering to rent his apartment for a week or two at a time — off the books.

Soni said he always declines, wary of running afoul of city rules but also because he prefers the security of operating through the Airbnb platform.

"We don't want to take any chances," he said.

Leovane went through the city's lengthy registration process to continue hosting short-term stays in his home. One of the biggest challenges: complying with the rule that he must remain in the home while hosting guests.

Since there is only one entrance to his home, Leovane had previously built an interior door inside the entryway that separated the downstairs area where he lives from the stairs that bring guests up to the space they rent on the second floor.

After the 2023 law took effect, city inspectors issued him a number of violations, including for the door, which he then had to tear down.

"Would you allow strangers in your house, with a door without a lock?" he said. "It doesn't make any sense."

One time a married couple who were staying for a week brought their two big German shepherds. The dogs ran up and down the stairs, barking, every time someone came to the front door. Leovane kept his distance as much as possible.

"They told me, 'the dogs don't bite, they're good dogs,'" he said. "But, hey, listen, I'm a stranger to those dogs. They don't know me."

Leovane, who said he relies on the revenue he earns through Airbnb to pay his bills, said he made about $11,000 last year. Before the city's crackdown, he pulled in about $30,000 a year.

Story says it takes a while for the place she's lived in for the last 30 years to feel like home again after her Airbnb guests leave. Her home's second unit has a long-term tenant, and Story vacates her own space when she gets a booking.

She stays with her partner or travels for at least a month, maybe two, in order to comply with the 30-day minimum stay rule. During that time, her guests are truly living in her home.

She had to set up automatic sprinklers to keep the outdoor plants alive. She often comes back to see the furniture's been rearranged. Once, someone threw away all her spices. Guests' left-behind socks and T-shirts surface weeks later.

"Five days or weeks at a time means it's still my home," she said. "If you're here for a month or two it becomes your place."

She bought the property, which once housed the 1980s-era nightclub, 8BC, in 1996. The building was in rough shape, and condemned a few years later. Story took out a large loan in 2003 to tear it down and rebuild.

"In the end, a lot of us are just people trying to get by, trying to keep our homes," she said.

Write to Kate King at kate.king@wsj.com

data.title: China Is Paying People to Shop. It's a Boom for Tech. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Tanner Brown

China is paying consumers to buy new things. It is also making some fairly specific suggestions about what those things should be.

Beijing has allocated 250 billion yuan, about $37 billion, this year for its consumer trade-in program. By August, the program had supported 1.55 trillion yuan in sales of eligible goods, according to the National Development and Reform Commission. The final installment went to local governments in late September.

It sounds like old-fashioned stimulus: Help households replace aging products and hope they keep spending. But the shopping list tells another story. China is using consumer subsidies to build markets for technologies it wants its factories to dominate, from artificial-intelligence glasses to energy-efficient appliances.

The results are strikingly uneven. Communications-equipment sales at larger retailers jumped 27.3% in August from a year earlier and 16.3% over the first eight months. Sales of smart glasses on major shopping platforms surged 120% during that period, according to the Commerce Ministry. Consumers purchased 108 million digital and smart products through the subsidy program.

The government is giving shoppers a reason to try gadgets that might otherwise remain novelties. Phones, tablets, smartwatches and smart glasses priced at 6,000 yuan or less qualify for a 15% subsidy, capped at 500 yuan per item. A 3,000-yuan pair of AI glasses, for example, can come with a 450-yuan discount. The program also covers six categories of appliances, but only models meeting the highest energy- or water-efficiency standards.

That selectivity is deliberate. At a government briefing, Vice Commerce Minister Sheng Qiuping described the strategy as using "new demand to guide new supply, and new supply to create new demand." Subsidies, he said, were designed to encourage purchases of greener appliances and vehicles.

This is industrial policy conducted at the checkout counter. Instead of simply putting money in households' pockets, Beijing rewards purchases that can help manufacturers increase production, bring down costs and cultivate entirely new product categories.

For investors, that creates opportunities beyond the brands displayed in stores. Chinese smartphone makers Huawei and Xiaomi are pursuing AI-enabled devices. Component manufacturers stand to benefit, too. Goertek, the Shenzhen-listed electronics supplier, told institutional investors in September that AI smart glasses could be "one of the categories with the greatest growth potential." It pointed to opportunities in optics, sensors, speakers and other components that make the devices work.

The implications for foreign companies are more complicated than a subsidy-driven victory for Chinese brands. The rules don't exclude Apple. Its qualifying iPhones can receive the same discount as domestic competitors, and Apple captured a 19% share of Chinese smartphone shipments in the second quarter, according to research firm Omdia, second only to Huawei.

Tesla can also benefit when buyers trade in eligible cars for qualifying electric vehicles. The subsidy for scrapping an older vehicle and buying an EV reaches 12% of the new car's price, up to 20,000 yuan. Yet selling cars has become harder for almost everyone.

Automobile retail sales by value plunged 18.5% in August, official data show. September brought a sharper warning: Domestic passenger-car sales by volume fell about 28%, according to industry figures. Electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids are taking a larger share of the market, but that doesn't mean the market itself is growing.

Tesla is now offering its own limited-time reductions of 5,000 yuan on the Model 3 and 7,000 yuan on the Model Y in China, underscoring how government help can coexist with bruising price competition.

The broader spending picture is hardly exuberant. Total retail sales grew just 0.4% in August. The value of subsidized product sales isn't the same as spending created by subsidies; plenty of customers would have bought those goods anyway.

And in the first eight months of last year, the trade-in program was associated with more than 2 trillion yuan in sales, versus 1.55 trillion yuan this year. The comparison isn't exact because Beijing narrowed eligibility in some categories. The central government also reduced annual funding from 300 billion yuan to 250 billion.

There is another risk: bringing purchases forward. A discounted smartphone bought this autumn may be one that a consumer would otherwise have purchased next spring. Subsidies can also shift spending away from restaurants, travel or other goods without persuading households to spend more overall.

"Consumers are expected to be more cautious about upgrading their devices," said Omdia analyst Hayden Hou.

That is the limit of Beijing's experiment. A government can make a new gadget cheaper and give its manufacturers a head start. Convincing cautious households to keep opening their wallets is a different challenge.

data.title: Cyber fraud alert: SBI warns about AI voice-cloning scams - 5 ways to protect your money
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- Advancements in voice-cloning technology are giving cybercriminals another way to impersonate family members, near and dear ones, friends, or officials and trick unsuspecting victims into transferring money or sharing sensitive information, resulting in unauthorised transactions.

A call that might sound like someone you know may not always be genuine. Especially in cases where the demand for funds is urgent and a fund transfer is requested immediately.

If you ever receive such a call, ensure that you never panic and carefully verify the facts and credentials before transferring any funds or following any instructions given in the call.

Highlighting this risk and its complications, the State Bank of India (SBI) has warned people about voice-cloning scams as part of its 'National Cyber Security Month Special Campaign 6.0'. In a post on X on 16 October 2026, the bank explained:

"National Cyber Security Month Special Campaign 6.0

Scammers can now clone voices to trick you!

Don't trust unexpected calls asking for money or personal information.Always verify before you act!

If in doubt, call back the person being impersonated for confirmation.

@DFS_India @DARPG_GoI @Cyberdost"

Along with this tweet, an informative video is attached to show how such scams, i.e., cyber frauds, are carried out. In the video, a fraudster calls Sunita, claiming to be her brother, 'Sonu', and asks for Rs.20,000, assuring her that he is her brother. Later, she is advised to first verify the facts by calling Sonu back before sending any money. This is how these scams are carried out.

Therefore, it is clear that voice-cloning scams may involve criminals using artificial intelligence (AI) to imitate a person's voice. Once the first step is complete and a call gets connected with the targeted victim, the fraudster may create urgency by claiming that a relative needs emergency funds or that an account requires immediate verification.

In such cases, acting in panic can lead victims to disclose confidential details or authorise fraudulent transactions, which can subsequently lead to serious financial losses.

1. Verify the caller's identity: Disconnect such calls immediately and call the person on their saved number to confirm the request. Never panic or act under pressure in such situations. Prudence is to verify facts diligently before acting.

2. Never rush money transfers: Treat all urgent requests for money, especially from unfamiliar numbers, with caution, even if the voice sounds familiar. This goes without exception; someone generally well-known will seldom ask for funds on an urgent basis without even having a proper conversation.

3. Never share confidential details: Do not disclose confidential data and information such as OTPs, PINs, passwords, CVV numbers or banking credentials over calls. These details are personal and confidential. They should never be discussed or disclosed with anyone, even from legitimate bank officials.

4. Use a family verification code: Agree on a private word or phrase with family members to help verify unusual emergency requests. This will require you to discuss such voice-cloning calls with family members and friends. Based on the awareness codes, strategies can be developed to sidestep such requests and protect your finances.

5. Report suspected fraud immediately: If money is lost, do not panic. Contact your bank immediately and call India's cybercrime helpline, 1930. You can also report the incident at cybercrime.gov.in.

In summary, awareness and proper vigilance are the best tools to combat such fraud, as these scams are rapidly evolving and spreading due to technological changes. Hence, as AI tools become more accessible and easier to use, recognising a familiar voice is no longer enough to establish complete trust.

It is vital for individuals to independently check and verify any unusual requests before sharing information or transferring money. A brief pause can help prevent a costly mistake and can also save an individual from financial losses, psychological stress and regret later on.

data.title: Trump waives some Russia oil sanctions, easing pressure on India
data.description:
NEW DELHI, Oct. 17 -- US President Donald Trump has waived key Russia-related sanctions and tariffs just days before they were due to take effect, offering potential relief to major buyers of Russian oil, including India and China.

In an executive order issued late on Friday, Trump said it was in the US "national interests" to withhold some of the sanctions. The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, signed by Trump last month, authorized him to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries importing Russian oil, with the aim of curbing Moscow's economic might amid its war with Ukraine.

The measures were due to take effect on 18 October.

The move comes as India and the US negotiate a trade deal that is said to be in its final stages, while crude oil prices remain above $100 a barrel amid the prolonged conflict in West Asia. The price surge poses a risk to India, which imports about 90% of its annual oil requirement, with Russia accounting for a substantial share of those supplies.

Earlier this month, Trump announced a decision to buy diesel from Moscow, aimed at curbing rising prices in the US.

The waiver could ease uncertainty around the India-US trade negotiations, as New Delhi seeks tariff concessions that give its exporters an advantage over competitors in the US market.

On Thursday, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said the first phase of the trade deal had been finalized and was being legally drafted. He expressed confidence that the agreement would be concluded and operationalised soon, but said India needed to secure an export advantage over its competitors in the US market.

The threat of US sanctions had introduced fresh uncertainty into the negotiations, leaving India unsure of the tariff concessions it could secure relative to competing countries that were not facing similar threats.

On Friday, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman expressed hope that the proposed trade deal would be concluded at the earliest, in the interest of both bilateral and global trade. Earlier this week, external affairs minister S. Jaishankar said the two sides were ironing out differences and moving towards a "landing point" in negotiations.

Separately, US ambassador to India Sergio Gor said earlier this week that negotiations were moving at an "incredible pace" and that the "big items are done".

In February, the two countries agreed on a framework for the deal that reduced the punitive tariff on most Indian goods to 18% from 50%. The higher tariff had been imposed in August 2025.

The US remains India's largest export market, accounting for $87 billion in goods exports in the fiscal year ended March 2026. In the first half of the current fiscal year, Indian exports to the US rose 11% from a year earlier to $50.8 billion, according to data from commerce ministry.

India is the second-largest importer of Russian oil after China, with Russian supplies forming a mainstay of its crude imports. In the April-July period, Russian oil supplies were valued at $28.33 billion, or about 45% of India's total oil imports of $63.33 billion, according to commerce ministry data.

Although the tariff threat did not significantly affect Russian oil supplies, as refiners struggled to replace those barrels immediately, the waiver could ease supply constraints and moderate prices. This comes amid persistent tensions in West Asia involving the US and Iran, as well as Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthi militia. These tensions have disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

For India, which relies heavily on imported crude, uncertainty over supplies and price volatility can have economy-wide consequences. Supply disruptions and geopolitical risks keep prices elevated, increasing costs for major importers such as India.

Global benchmark Brent crude traded at $72 a barrel in February, before the US-Iran war erupted, peaking at $130 a barrel in April. Prices are currently at $109.9 a barrel.

The country's crude oil import bill stood at around $123 billion in fiscal year 2026 (FY26), according to data from the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell. A sustained increase of $1 a barrel is estimated to raise the annual bill by Rs.18,000 crore, estimates from Bank of Baroda show.

India has already imported crude worth $74.85 billion in the first five months of the current fiscal year, equivalent to about 48% of its total import bill for FY26, Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell data showed.

A higher import bill could add to inflationary pressures if the increased costs are passed on to downstream products and consumers. It could also weigh on economic growth and widen pressure on the current account.

India's retail inflation rose to a 23-month high of 5.54% in September. In October, the Reserve Bank of India raised its inflation projection for FY27 to 5.2%, from 5% in August, citing volatility in international oil prices, persistent supply-side pressures stemming from deficient south-west monsoon rainfall.

data.title: Peter Schiff Sounds Alarm On Inflation, Housing And Banks — ‘We’re Actually Even Closer Now To An Even Bigger Crisis’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Schiff sees particular risks in housing, where millions of mortgages originated when rates were far below today's levels.
  • The economist warned that mortgage rates could eventually climb toward 9%, putting further pressure on housing affordability and potentially forcing home prices significantly lower.
  • Schiff added that higher rates and falling property values could create losses across the financial system, particularly if borrowers begin defaulting.

Economist Peter Schiff is sounding the alarm over rising inflation, higher interest rates and growing financial stress, warning that the U.S. economy could be heading toward a much bigger crisis.

During a recent episode of his podcast, Schiff argued that investors are underestimating the risks created by persistent inflation and a Federal Reserve caught between fighting prices and protecting the financial system.

Housing And Banks Could Be The Next Breaking Point, Warns Schiff

Schiff's biggest concern is what happens if interest rates continue rising in an economy that has become heavily dependent on cheap credit. He sees particular risks in housing, where millions of mortgages originated when rates were far below today's levels.

"We're actually even closer now to an even bigger crisis," Schiff said.

He warned that mortgage rates could eventually climb toward 9%, putting further pressure on housing affordability and potentially forcing home prices significantly lower. Higher rates and falling property values could create losses across the financial system, particularly if borrowers begin defaulting.

Schiff believes the resulting downturn could ultimately be worse than the 2008 financial crisis.

Gold The 'Last Safe Haven Standing’, Says Schiff

Schiff sees gold as one of the few assets that can protect investors if inflation remains elevated while confidence in government debt deteriorates.

"Gold is the last safe haven standing," Schiff said, while arguing that higher Treasury yields are not necessarily bearish for gold. If yields rise because investors demand greater compensation for inflation and fiscal risk, the move can instead reinforce the case for precious metals.

Schiff believes that investors should focus less on nominal interest rates and more on real purchasing power. If inflation rises faster than bond yields, holders of fixed-income assets can still lose money in inflation-adjusted terms.

“That's why you buy gold. Gold is the only hedge against treasuries and bonds and gilts and all these other sovereign debt instruments,” he added.

Schiff Warns Inflation Could Hit 7% In 2027

Schiff's most aggressive warning concerns inflation, where he argued that recent price data could be the beginning of a much larger acceleration rather than a temporary bump.

September's CPI rose 0.6% from the prior month, putting the annual rate at 3.7%. But Schiff believes inflation could accelerate substantially from here, potentially reaching 7% or higher in 2027 and remaining elevated into 2028.

This, Schiff believes, would put the Fed in an increasingly difficult position. Raising rates aggressively could trigger the housing and financial crisis Schiff fears, while failing to raise rates could allow inflation to become even more entrenched.

He also warned that markets may be preparing for the wrong problem. Investors are focused on whether the Fed will cut or hike rates, Schiff says, while the bigger risk could be a combination of higher inflation, higher borrowing costs and financial instability.

If that scenario unfolds, Schiff believes the fallout could be far larger than markets currently anticipate.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, declined 0.26; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) edged lower by 0.27%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) fell 0.21%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘bearish’ territory at the time of writing.

The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) gained 0.1% on Friday, while the iShares 7-10 Year Treasury Bond ETF (IEF) rose 0.08%.

data.title: India's food regulator proposes ban on added sugars in infant foods
data.description:
India's food safety regulator on Saturday proposed a ban on adding sucrose and fructose to food products for infants up to six months of age, tightening rules on added sugars in infant nutrition products.

Under existing rules, lactose and glucose polymers are the preferred carbohydrate sources in infant nutrition products, while sucrose and fructose can be added when required, subject to prescribed limits, the regulator said.

The move comes amid an intensifying food safety crackdown in India, where regulators have forced local eateries and branded restaurants to suspend operations, while a push for front-of-pack warning labels has rattled the country's more than $100 billion packaged food industry.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said the proposed measure aims to reduce infants' exposure to added sugars and address health risks linked to childhood obesity.

The existing regulations set nutritional composition, quality and safety standards for infant nutrition products intended for children from birth to 24 months of age, it said.

Activists and officials have long raised concerns about rising obesity rates, particularly among children. India had 180 million overweight or obese adults in 2021, a figure projected to reach 450 million by 2050, according to a study published in the medical journal The Lancet.

The FSSAI and some state regulators have intensified checks on food safety in recent months, releasing regular public updates including photos and videos of raids that have ​drawn widespread attention online.

In August, the FSSAI proposed a red hexagonal stamp on labels of food products high in any two or more nutrients of concern such as sugar, salt or saturated fat, but tightened the proposal after a public outcry, saying a warning would now be required if even one nutrient exceeds the prescribed level.

data.title: Why Renault is betting on hybrids in EV 'outlier' India
data.description:
NEW DELHI, Oct. 17 -- When Stephane Deblaise took charge of Renault's India operations a little over a year ago, he brought a lesson from South Korea: car buyers do not necessarily replace their petrol or diesel cars with electric vehicles (EVs).

His first year in India has reinforced that view. Buyers still weigh engine performance, fuel efficiency, technology and price before choosing a car, the 54-year-old French chief executive told Mint. "The big picture I understood very quickly," he said. "Engines are very important. Value is very important."

That conviction is now shaping Renault's biggest powertrain bet yet on the Indian market: a strong hybrid version of its flagship sport utility vehicle (SUV), the Duster, launched on Saturday.

India's electrification story has so far been led by battery EVs, with strong hybrids lagging behind. EV penetration in passenger vehicles rose to about 8.5% in September from 5.7% a year earlier, according to Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (Fada) data. Strong hybrids, by contrast, have remained at around 2%.

EVs accounted for one-fifth of incremental growth in the car market in fiscal year 2026 (FY26), with electric car sales surging 84% to nearly 200,000 units. Strong hybrids, offered in India by Japanese carmakers Maruti Suzuki, Toyota Kirloskar and Honda Cars, remain a much smaller segment.

But the global experience suggests that the transition away from conventional engines need not be an all-electric one.

In the US, hybrids accounted for 16% of the market in the second quarter of 2026, against 6% for EVs, according to the US Energy Information Administration. In the European Union, hybrids made up 36.6% of new car registrations in the first eight months of 2026, compared with a 21.7% share for battery EVs, according to the European Automobile Manufacturers' Association.

"Even the most advanced country for BEV is not only BEV," Deblaise said.

He argues that the pace of adoption depends as much on policy and customer preferences as on technology. "The percentages are only depending on policies. They are depending on policies and customer appetite."

"The BEV is relatively high these days. It's a huge gap. But it is helped by the 5% tax. If we would not have 5%, it would be 0.5%," he said.

India charges 5% goods and services tax (GST) on EVs, while hybrids have not received equivalent treatment, with these vehicles-mostly large SUVs-taxed at 40%.

For Deblaise, the bigger question is whether customers can adopt electric mobility without compromising on convenience. Charging infrastructure and the time needed to recharge remain constraints, he said. "A car, it is freedom. But a BEV car, today, it is not freedom."

Hybrids offer a way to improve fuel economy without requiring buyers to change how they use their cars. That is the opportunity Renault hopes to exploit with the Duster Strong Hybrid, its first full-hybrid offering in India.

The SUV's 1.8-litre powertrain and 1.4-kWh battery deliver a claimed mileage of 29 km per litre, allowing Renault to pitch it against diesel SUVs that have traditionally attracted buyers seeking fuel efficiency.

"29 kilometres per litre in hybrid is a game changer in India. There is no doubt. Our strong tech hybrid is the new diesel," Deblaise said.

The proposition, however, comes with a price trade-off. Hybrid powertrains cost more than conventional petrol and diesel systems, making the upfront purchase price a key hurdle in a market where value remains central to buying decisions. Renault is banking on localization to improve the economics over time.

Deblaise said the company had spent nearly a decade developing the technology, including its battery and gearbox. "We are not trying to introduce innovation in India to check if our idea is good. We have already done it," he said.

Deblaise's confidence in hybrids draws partly on an earlier decision in South Korea, where engineering constraints prevented Renault from launching hybrid and internal-combustion engine (ICE) versions of a new car simultaneously.

He chose to launch the hybrid first. "I said, okay, we launch first the hybrid," he recalled.

The hybrid eventually accounted for 92% of the car's volumes over its lifecycle, despite a relatively high price gap between the two versions. Deblaise said the result did not mean customers had rejected conventional engines.

"There was nothing against ICE. But we had a very good solution on hybrid," he said.

He does not expect India to replicate South Korea's 92% share. But he believes hybrids can account for a meaningful portion of Renault's sales. "We should have a big part of our volumes. A big two-digit percentage of our volumes in hybrid," he said.

The bet comes as Renault seeks to revive its fortunes in India. According to Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (Siam) data, Renault's sales rose 32% to 23,122 units in April-September 2026, when the Duster rolled out.

Whether the hybrid strategy can sustain that recovery remains an open question. Deblaise acknowledged that offering customers more choice may not be enough to bring every former or potential buyer back to the brand.

"Some people maybe will never come in Renault because they don't want. It will take time for them to come."

data.title: The Fed Will Have to Raise Interest Rates More, Even If It Pauses in October — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Nicole Goodkind

Federal Reserve officials appear inclined to keep interest rates unchanged at their Oct. 27-28 policy meeting. But don't be fooled by a pause: More rate increases are likely coming, possibly as soon as December, to tame escalating inflation.

The Fed raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter of a percentage point in September, to a target range of 3.75%-4.00%, its first increase since 2023. Officials have since indicated that they want more time to assess the economy before making another move.

There is plenty to assess, and some of it isn't encouraging.

The consumer price index rose 3.7% in September from a year earlier. That was a stronger-than-expected increase and a sizable jump up from August's 3.4% annual growth rate. Prices climbed o.6% month to month in September, with a 9.1% jump in gasoline accounting for more than half the increase. Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, accelerated to 2.6% annually from 2.4% in August.

There were signs of broader price pressures, too. Airfares, education, recreation, and used vehicles all became more expensive.

Producer prices surged 1.3% in September, their largest monthly gain in four years. Wholesale prices were up 6.3% from a year earlier, raising concerns that businesses could pass additional costs on to consumers in the coming months.

The numbers strengthened the case for higher interest rates, but markets don't think the latest data changed the Fed's apparent preference for waiting until later this year to raise rates. The latest reports make a December increase more likely, said James McCann at Edward Jones. He expects one increase in 2027, as well.

"The Fed won't panic in the face of these numbers, but the data will add to the conviction on the FOMC [Federal Open Market Committee] that policy needs to be tighter to help drag inflation back to target," he wrote in a note Friday.

Inflation has run above the Fed's 2% annual target for more than five years. Central bank officials spent the week explaining why they are concerned about inflation without committing to an immediate rise in rates.

Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee called Wednesday's CPI report discouraging. But in an interview with Yahoo Finance, he cautioned against placing too much weight on a single report.

"I don't think we yet know the answer to that," he said when asked if more rate hikes are needed. But "if we get more months like this...that's totally unacceptable," he said of the inflation report.

Speaking in Bangkok on Wednesday, Fed governor Michelle Bowman said she saw no urgency to adjust rates again. "We have some time to wait and see how financial conditions evolve before we take more action," she said.

San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly suggested that further tightening would probably be needed but not at the next meeting. "Why force urgency when you don't need to have urgency?" Daly said Wednesday in an interview with Reuters. "We have more meetings ahead of us."

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack offered an argument for acting sooner, however. In remarks Monday, she warned that inflation is becoming increasingly broad-based and that businesses are beginning to incorporate higher costs into their pricing plans. "When feasible, I generally think it's preferable to make smaller adjustments, and to do so relatively quickly, rather than to wait and risk needing a larger course correction," Hammack said at the meeting of the National Association for Business Economics (NABE) in Cleveland, Ohio.

On Thursday, speaking at an event held by Goldman Sachs, she warned that deteriorating inflation expectations could require more aggressive rate increases. The warning caused some to speculate that a half-percentage-point increase is on the table later this year.

The Fed's Beige Book, released Wednesday, showed economic growth slowing in parts of the country, with hiring subdued and lower-income consumers pulling back on spending. Businesses reported rising costs from energy and tariffs, and noted that customers were becoming less able to absorb higher prices.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh offered little indication Thursday evening that the latest data had changed his thinking. Speaking in Bangkok, he said economic developments since the September meeting had matched the Fed's expectations.

"I don't prejudge meetings," Warsh said.

Investors took his comments as another reason to expect a pause. They are now pricing in an 83% chance that rates remain unchanged at the October meeting, according to the CME FedWatch tool. Expectations for an increase had briefly surged following Wednesday's inflation report.

The Fed's October meeting will take place less than a week before the midterm elections.

Research by CME Group's Mark Shore found that the Fed left interest rates unchanged between Oct. 1 and Election Day in about two-thirds of election years from 1972 through 2024.

This past week's data and Fed speakers suggest more monetary tightening might be merited later in the year, but the September increase may have bought the Fed some time.

For now, investors and economists are looking past October to a possible December increase.

data.title: Renault Duster Strong Hybrid takes on Toyota, Maruti Suzuki with ₹16.99 lakh price, 29 km/l mileage
data.description:
Renault’s Duster Strong Hybrid E-Tech 160 enters India’s strong-hybrid passenger-vehicle market, estimated at 1.23 lakh units in FY26, with a starting price of ₹16.99 lakh and claimed mileage of 29 km/l. The French automaker is targeting diesel SUV buyers as it challenges Toyota and Maruti Suzuki.

With Renault’s retail market share below 1 per cent, the Duster must convert its fuel-efficiency advantage into sustained sales against established Toyota and Maruti Suzuki hybrids and diesel SUVs backed by stronger dealership networks and customer loyalty.

The Duster is priced ₹31,000 above the entry-level Maruti Suzuki Grand Vitara Strong Hybrid at ₹16.68 lakh and broadly in line with Toyota’s Urban Cruiser Hyryder Strong Hybrid, priced from around ₹16.81 to 17.18 lakh. However, its 1.8-litre petrol engine and dual-motor system deliver 160 PS, against 116 PS from the 1.5-litre hybrid systems in both rivals. Renault also claims better mileage than their 27.97 km/l, while its 1.4-kWh battery enables electric-only operation for up to 80 per cent of city driving time, depending on conditions.

Speaking to reporters after the launch, Renault Group India Chief Executive Officer Stéphane Deblaise said the hybrid would expand the Duster’s customer base beyond its petrol variants, allowing it to compete more directly for diesel SUV buyers.

Strong-hybrid registrations rose 9.5 per cent to 86,403 units during January–September 2026, from 78,881 a year earlier, according to previously compiled vehicle-registration data. Despite the growth, the category remains a small part of India’s passenger-vehicle market.

Diesel alternative

During the media roundtable, Deblaise positioned strong hybrids as an alternative to diesel vehicles, citing fuel efficiency, lower total cost of ownership and driving refinement. He said consumers could not move overnight from internal-combustion vehicles to battery-electric cars.

Renault said it has sold more than one million vehicles equipped with its hybrid technology globally, providing an established technology base for its India introduction.

Product offensive

The launch is part of Renault’s seven-model roadmap through 2030, spanning petrol, CNG, strong-hybrid and electric vehicles across two platforms. The company is preparing the sub-four-metre Bridger SUV for late 2027, followed by an electric model expected in 2028.

Management, however, clarified that there are no immediate plans to introduce the Duster’s hybrid system in smaller models such as the Kwid, Triber and Kiger. Adapting the technology would require significant engineering and packaging changes, Deblaise said.

Renault is also expanding its CNG offerings and targeting up to 90 per cent localisation across future product programmes to improve cost competitiveness. It has outlined an ambition of €2 billion in annual exports by 2030, covering vehicles, components and engineering services.

Ownership challenge

Beyond pricing and efficiency, Renault must address concerns over hybrid maintenance, battery reliability, spare-parts costs and service accessibility.

During the post-launch interaction, Deblaise acknowledged gaps in service infrastructure and parts pricing, saying Renault was examining additional localisation opportunities while strengthening existing facilities and dealer training.

With Renault’s retail market share below 1 per cent, the Duster must convert its fuel-efficiency advantage into sustained sales against established Toyota and Maruti Suzuki hybrids and diesel SUVs backed by stronger dealership networks and customer loyalty.

data.title: Jindal Ferrous Enters Carbon Steel Market With Rs 5,000 Cr Odisha Plant
data.description:
The 2.2 million tonne facility brings integrated steelmaking, automation and waste recycling under one roof as the company expands its presence in the domestic carbon steel market

Jindal Ferrous has entered integrated carbon steel manufacturing with a Rs 5,000 crore investment in Jajpur, Odisha. The new facility, inaugurated by Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi on 14 October 2026, can produce 2.2 million tonnes of steel annually.

The plant gives the company a production base to serve customers across India, particularly in the northern and eastern regions, where infrastructure projects and industrial activity support demand for carbon steel. Its immediate priority is to ramp up operations and establish a customer base.

Integrated Steelmaking Operations

The Jajpur facility combines a sinter plant, blast furnace, steel melting shop, and supporting infrastructure. By housing these operations at one location, Jindal Ferrous can manage several stages of steel production within the same complex.

Resource recovery also forms part of the plant’s operating design. The facility processes metallurgical waste through its sinter plant and reuses process gases, measures intended to improve material utilisation and limit waste generation.

The blast furnace incorporates a Level-2 automation platform, an expert model, high top-pressure operation and dry gas-cleaning systems. These technologies are designed to support process control, production stability and operating efficiency.

International Technology Support

The company has partnered with Japan’s JFE Steel Corporation for technical support during the plant’s operational ramp-up and steel production.

Several international suppliers have contributed equipment and technology. Germany’s SMS Group, through Paul Wurth, supplied the blast furnace technology. Sweden’s UHT provided the Granshot system, while Austria’s Primetals Technologies supplied technology for the sinter plant, basic oxygen furnace shop and caster. Italy’s Danieli provided equipment for the ladle furnace and hot-metal desulphurisation system.

These partnerships support the company’s effort to establish integrated steelmaking operations and achieve reliable production as the facility moves towards its intended operating levels.

Building A Steel Cluster

The investment adds another manufacturing facility to the Jindal group’s presence in Jajpur. Jindal Stainless has increased its production capacity at the site from 0.8 million tonnes to 2.2 million tonnes over the past two decades, according to the company.

The group is also pursuing plans to expand the industrial ecosystem around its operations. Jindal Stainless has laid the foundation for a proposed stainless steel park covering more than 270 acres. The park is designed to host over 180 downstream and ancillary units, with the potential to create more than 15,000 jobs.

A Centre of Excellence is also planned to develop skills, support technology adoption and strengthen downstream manufacturing. The proposed park could create business opportunities for suppliers, logistics operators, maintenance providers and other ancillary businesses as the industrial cluster develops. The extent of these opportunities will depend on the establishment of downstream units and supporting services.

Because an Indian ED order cannot directly block a Georgia land registry, New Delhi must now frantically activate Mutual Legal Assistance Treaties (MLAT) to halt the transaction before the Mahadev betting loot vanishes into the American financial system forever.

The London Conspiracy & The Master Architect

Behind the clinical terminology of this corporate takeover lay a series of clandestine, high-stakes meetings in London. The SkyExchange Mirage and the Hawala Pipeline

The money was routed back into India via sophisticated financial instruments—including Qualified Institutional Placements (QIPs), Foreign Portfolio Investments (FPIs), and Foreign Direct Investments (FDIs)—pumped directly into listed entities controlled by Garg.

From Rs 13 Penny Stock to a $361 Million Global Empire

The most spectacular illusion in this financial thriller was the meteoric, logic-defying rise of Justride Enterprises, a virtually unknown penny stock trading at a measly Rs 13. data.title: India's ICICI Bank Q2 profit rises 20.1%, beats estimates
data.description:
By Ashwin Manikandan

Indian private lender ICICI Bank reported a higher-than-expected profit for its second quarter on Saturday, driven by stronger loan demand and lower provisions for bad loans.

The country's second-largest private lender by market capitalisation posted a standalone net profit of 148.43 billion Indian rupees ($1.56 billion) for the three months ended September, compared with 123.59 billion rupees a year earlier.

Analysts had expected a profit of 142.51 billion rupees, according to data compiled by LSEG.

Indian lenders have seen strong loan growth during the quarter across both corporate and retail segments.

ICICI Bank's net interest income rose 17.7% to 253.39 billion rupees, aided by a 30% increase in total loans. Deposits grew 27.1% from a year earlier.

Its net interest margin, a key measure of profitability, narrowed to 4.18% from 4.36% in the previous quarter.

Funds kept aside for potential bad loans and other losses fell 6.9% to 8.51 billion rupees.

The bank's other income, which includes income from bonds and other investments, rose 6.2% to 80.47 billion rupees amid volatile currency and debt markets.

The lender's asset quality improved, with the gross non-performing asset ratio at 1.20% at the end of September, compared with 1.38% in the prior three months.

data.title: Indian state food safety authority names Blinkit, Reliance executives in expired food probe
data.description:
By Arpan Chaturvedi

India's food safety authority has named officials of Reliance Group entities and of Eternal’s Blinkit and Hyperpure units, including Blinkit CEO Albinder Dhindsa, in a probe over expired food products that have allegedly re-entered the food supply chain, according to case documents reviewed by Reuters.

The Food and Drug Administration of Maharashtra state, home to Mumbai, has led a crackdown on food safety under its chief Tukaram Mundhe, 51, including shutting down some of Mumbai’s most popular eateries as well as outlets of Domino’s and Pizza Hut for poor hygiene. The state agency has also suspended the permit of a McDonald’s outlet.

The latest case, which has led to a police complaint by the food safety authority, involves large retail and quick-commerce companies, which sell products to millions of households in the world’s most populous country.

Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration, according to the documents reviewed by Reuters, said its officials visited some warehouses of Reliance Retail, Reliance Consumer and Zomato Hyperpure, and that company officials could not provide verifiable proof that disposal of expired food was actually carried out by their contractors.

"The disposal agencies ... do not destroy the stock," the case document alleged.

In the case of a Zomato Hyperpure warehouse, a company representative named a contractor as its disposal agency which FDA officials could not trace, according to the documents.

Reliance and Blinkit did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

"Any attempt to divert expired, damaged or consumer-rejected food products meant for destruction back into the market is a serious matter that demands strict scrutiny and accountability," Maharashtra's FDA chief Tukaram Mundhe told Reuters.

"No company, brand, business or individual is above the law when it comes to food safety."

INDIA'S INTENSIFYING CRACKDOWN

Reliance Retail and Reliance Consumer are part of billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s business group. Zomato’s Hyperpure is a unit of Eternal that also runs food delivery service Zomato and quick commerce business Blinkit.

The FDA probe said it found a pattern where large retail and quick commerce distribution warehouses handed over expired and customer-rejected packages of food to contractors who passed the food to unlicensed sorting yards. These sorting yards then separated out saleable-looking packets, which eventually reached other retailers and the consumer market, according to case documents from the probe.

"The chain thus runs from company warehouse to disposal agency, unlicensed yard, broker, retailer and consumer."

The Maharashtra FDA on Thursday suspended the licences of five establishments in the state — three Reliance and two Eternal entities, the case documents said.

Enforcement of food safety laws has traditionally been weak in India and the recent round of extensive crackdowns has garnered large-scale public support.

In August, Indian authorities raided an illegal operation in Mumbai that faked expiry dates and nutritional information on original food products manufactured by PepsiCo , Nestle , Coca-Cola and Unilever, so they could be exported to other countries.

data.title: Judge Rejects Gemini And CFTC Bid To Overturn $5 Million Settlement
data.description:
TL;DR: A federal judge has rejected a joint attempt by Gemini and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to overturn the exchange’s $5 million settlement. The decision leaves the existing judgment in place despite the regulator’s changed approach to cryptocurrency enforcement.

Gemini has failed in an unusual attempt to undo a regulatory settlement, despite having the very agency that brought the original case on its side.

US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein rejected a joint motion by the exchange and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission seeking to vacate a consent judgment entered in January 2025.

The settlement arose from allegations that Gemini misled the regulator during its review of a proposed Bitcoin futures product in 2017. Gemini agreed to pay a $5 million penalty and accepted a permanent injunction.

When Regulators Change Their Minds

The CFTC subsequently reconsidered the original enforcement case as its digital asset priorities evolved. Together with Gemini, it asked the court to revisit the settlement.

That is a very different situation from the more familiar legal battle in which an exchange disputes a regulator’s allegations. This time, both parties wanted relief from the court’s earlier judgment.

But a change in enforcement policy does not automatically erase a final court order. The judge found that the arguments presented did not satisfy the legal standards for reopening the settlement.

The decision is significant for other cryptocurrency businesses hoping that a more accommodating federal regulatory environment might undo historical enforcement outcomes.

What Changes For Gemini?

In the immediate term, very little. The settlement remains in effect and the court has not imposed a new fine.

The wider message is more important: courts retain control of their judgments, even when a regulatory agency changes its view of a case.

Washington’s approach to cryptocurrency may have become more favourable, but companies cannot assume that previously approved settlements will disappear alongside the political circumstances in which they were reached.
